profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is the Manasquan Cable Landing Station, tagged here as Apollo, one of the US landing points for the Apollo transatlantic submarine cable system owned and operated by Vodafone Group, a British multinational telecommunications company headquartered in Newbury, Berkshire, England. Apollo provides two geographically diverse fiber optic paths across the Atlantic between the United States and Europe, with a second US landing site in Shirley, New York; its cable segments connect onward to major data center hubs including New York City, Washington DC, and Ashburn, Virginia. This is a distinct facility from the nearby Manasquan TAT-14 cable landing station recorded elsewhere in this registry under the Sprint operator record, since multiple submarine cable systems commonly cluster their US landing points along the same stretch of New Jersey coastline. As a cable landing station rather than a general purpose colocation facility, no critical IT megawattage figure was found or would be expected to be published. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading: Vodafone Group is a British multinational telecommunications company with its registered headquarters in Newbury, Berkshire, England. Vodafone owns and operates the Apollo transatlantic submarine cable system, which provides two geographically diverse fiber optic paths across the Atlantic Ocean between the United States and Europe. The facility linked to this operator record, the Manasquan Cable Landing Station tagged here as Apollo, is one of Apollo's US landing points, alongside a separate landing site in Shirley, New York; Apollo's cable segments connect onward to major data center hubs including New York City, Washington DC, and Ashburn, Virginia. This is a distinct facility from the nearby Manasquan TAT-14 cable landing station referenced elsewhere in this registry under the Sprint operator record, since multiple submarine cable systems commonly cluster their US landing points along the same stretch of New Jersey coastline for similar reasons of subsea geography and existing conduit infrastructure. As a cable landing station rather than a general purpose colocation facility, no critical IT megawattage figure was found or would be expected to be published for this Vodafone facility.
